question: Who is designated as the sacrificial animal within the Kula tradition?
premises: The one situated in the midst of the yoginī group is identified.
That one is called the animal.
This designation is made within the Kula.
inference: In the Kula tradition, the one placed in the midst of the yoginī group is called the sacrificial animal.
uncertainties: Gender agreement between paśuḥ and kīrtitaṃ is irregular in the transmitted text.
plain_english: In the Kula, he who is situated in the midst of the group of yoginīs is called the animal.
